recipes.name: Pancit Molo (Filipino Wonton Soup)
ingredients_raw: 1 pound uncooked medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 (8 ounce) can sliced water chestnuts, drained
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 (16 ounce) package wonton wrappers, or as needed
1 small head bok choy, cut into bite-sized pieces

steps.text: Mix pork, shrimp, water chestnuts, salt, and pepper together in a large bowl. Reserve 1/3 of the filling mixture for soup. Wrap about 1 tablespoon of remaining filling in a wonton wrapper. Repeat until all filling is used up.

Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add onion and garlic; sauté until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in chicken and reserved filling. Mix well. Add chicken broth; season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Drop filled wontons into soup one by one. Boil until wontons float to the top, 3 to 5 minutes. Add bok choy; boil until tender, about 2 minutes more. Garnish with green onions.

raw_recipe.headline: Pancit Molo (Filipino Wonton Soup)
raw_recipe.description: Rather than noodles, this Filipino pancit soup includes yummy wontons full of pork, prawns, and water chestnuts, plus chicken and bok choy.

review.reviewBody: I made it for the first time as a Filipino, cooked for my little children and they LOVED it so much they asked me to cook it weekly. This is the easiest recipe to follow but the flavour is just as exemplary as I remembered it from when I was in Grade 5, when I first tasted it in our Home Economics class in the Philippines. No one in my family cooks it so I didn't taste it again until now, abroad, where I'm 34 and yearning to make the soup from a fond memory however other website recipes called for harder and longer methods (ie. making chicken broth from scratch--no thank you!) that were not feasible for my situation. So I was really happy to have found your recipe. Also, the water chestnuts are THE BOMB! It provides such amazing flavour and texture. Don't skip it! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND this recipe and THANK YOU EVER SO MUCH TO THE AUTHOR FOR SHARING IT. Now I finally have a recipe to pass down from one generation to another, with the proper citation of sources, of course. God bless us all!
I used ground turkey instead of pork and left out water chestnuts. Only used about a teaspoon of filling and boiled them 5-7 minutes. Turned out great.
